summary: Remote agent exposes installer host to arbitrary shell, filesystem, and git operations over a WebSocket channel
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent@1.0.188 is a remote agent that opens a WebSocket to a configured server URL and dispatches server-sent messages to privileged handlers on the installer's host. `terminal_input` frames are written directly into a spawned PTY running the user's default shell (`process.env.SHELL || 'bash'`, PowerShell/cmd on Windows), allowing the remote peer to execute arbitrary commands. The same message router also exposes `read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `upload_to_dir`, `git_add/reset/restore/commit/push`, and `proxy_request` handlers, giving the WebSocket peer read/write access to arbitrary files, control over local git repositories (including push), and the ability to proxy HTTP/WS traffic through the host. Whoever controls the configured server URL therefore has full remote-administration of the installer's machine when the agent is running. Additional install-side behavior: `service/linux.js` modifies shell PATH to include `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin`, and `yeaft/tools/web-search.js` invokes `ping` and outbound `POST` requests.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
